marketSession: 14 October Malaysia early morning, after completed Tuesday 13 October US regular session, before US September CPI
title: AI Chips Fall. Is the Market Finally Questioning the Bill?
intro: US stocks barely moved on Tuesday, but semiconductor shares continued to look weaker. The broad US benchmark closed at 7,805.45, down just 0.02%, and the Nasdaq slipped 0.15%. Meanwhile, the semiconductor ETF SMH fell 0.49% to 588.12.

sections.label: Where Is the Money Coming From?
sections.text: Steve Eisman is worried about the way money moves around the AI industry.
paragraphs: Steve Eisman is worried about the way money moves around the AI industry. OpenAI and Anthropic promise to spend heavily on computing power. Cloud companies build data centres for them, and some of those same cloud and chip companies also invest in the labs.
The arrangement can work if enough independent customers pay to use the AI. If those payments cannot keep up, someone will eventually have to borrow more, spend less or delay a project.

Big orders are not the same thing as profit. Oracle's backlog is enormous, yet future contracts must still turn into actual cash. On the other hand, Microsoft reported positive free cash flow last quarter, so it would be wrong to say every AI company has already run out of money.

sections.label: What About the Picks and Shovels?
sections.text: Power and electrical equipment have a more physical demand story.
paragraphs: Power and electrical equipment have a more physical demand story. Data centres need turbines, transformers, switchgear, cooling and fast network connections before anyone can use an AI model.

That is why GE Vernova, Eaton and network companies such as Arista deserve attention. They can sell equipment to multiple operators. But it is still important to ask whether customers can finance the construction and whether the share price already assumes years of growth.

Micron and Nvidia remain central to the buildout, although the memory and chip trade is much more sensitive to customers slowing their orders. I would rather see current earnings, cash and the share price agree before chasing that weakness.

sections.label: Why Are Yields Still Important?
sections.text: Borrowing remains expensive even after bonds found some relief.
paragraphs: Borrowing remains expensive even after bonds found some relief. Reports on Tuesday placed the US 10-year yield around 5.22% and the 30-year near 5.56%. That is a high hurdle for data centres and other businesses relying on money they hope to earn years from now.

Oil has also been volatile because of the Middle East conflict and changing fuel supply expectations. A fresh rise in energy prices could keep inflation sticky, limiting relief for long-term borrowing rates.

sections.label: What Would Change My View?
sections.text: CPI arrives on 14 October, then PPI and TSMC earnings on 15 October.
paragraphs: CPI arrives on Wednesday, 14 October, followed by PPI and TSMC results on Thursday. A softer inflation print would be more encouraging if Treasury yields and credit conditions respond, rather than stocks merely bouncing for an hour.

For the AI trade, I want to see real orders and cash conversion hold up, especially in memory, cloud services and power equipment. If customers start cutting orders while financing costs rise, the warning becomes much more serious.

verdict: My view: the AI investment cycle is still active, but the easy part of the trade may be behind us. I would favour financially sound suppliers and wait for a clearer price entry until paid demand and funding are better proven.
